pure-announcement.rationale: It is a project landing page describing an established framework, not a launch, release note or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: osv-format is the only nearby supply-chain concept and it covers vulnerability interchange, not build-integrity assurance levels.

unfalsifiable.rationale: SLSA is a public OpenSSF specification the note links directly, so its central claims are checkable even though the testimonial statistics are unsourced.

durability.rationale: The framework it names is durable, but the capture holds only marketing copy — that SLSA exists, has four unspecified levels, and has industry backers — with none of the level requirements that would stay useful in a year.

actionability.rationale: It orients a reader toward using SLSA levels as a common yardstick but contains no requirement, control or step — every actionable detail lives behind its 'read the specifications' links.

atomicity.rationale: It is a single idea — a leveled security framework for supply-chain artifact integrity — easily stated in one paragraph.
